2. Symmetries

Source: vignettes/articles/guide-symmetries.Rmd
guide-symmetries.Rmd

If a continuous family of parameter values gives the same prediction for every observable, no data of these observables can tell the members apart. symmetryDetection(), through the Python package symident, finds such families in the model of Setting up models; they are removed before the fit. Code: symmetries.R and the end of model.R.

Lie symmetries and detection

Such a family is the orbit of a Lie symmetry with a generator, a vector field on the parameters. Most symmetries of reaction networks are scalings: the moved parameters are multiplied by powers of one factor, and on log scale an orbit is a straight line. symident obtains the generators as the kernel of the observability-identifiability matrix, built from the Lie derivatives of the observables, and proves scalings exactly; see Methods > Structural identifiability and Lie symmetries.

Detection settings

  • equilibrate = TRUE: the cells start at the steady state without TNFα, so initial values are functions of the parameters.
  • reduceCQ = TRUE: one species per conserved moiety is eliminated, symmetries act on the totals, the parameters of Pimpl().
  • forcings = "TNF": TNFα is an input state, 0 at rest and set by the event at time 0.
  • conditions: the two doses; a direction is non-identifiable only if it is so in both.

The imaging readouts bleach, \(y = \log(s x + o) - \tau t\); \(e^{-\tau t}\) is no function of the states of a model at rest. In the control the states are constant and the slope of an imaging readout is \(-\tau\) alone, so the bleaching rates are in no symmetry, and symmetries.R drops the bleaching terms.

Symmetries of the full model 

# at rest without TNFα, which an event adds at time 0 in the stimulated condition; the moieties
# of NFκB and IKK by their totals, the parameters of Pimpl()
doses <- data.frame(dose_TNF = c(0, 1), row.names = c("control", "TNF"))
# without the bleaching terms: in the resting control the states are constant, and the slope of
# an imaging readout is the bleaching rate alone
unbleached <- eqnvec(sub(" - tau_.*$", "", observables), names = names(observables))
symmetries <- symmetryDetection(reactions, unbleached, events = events, forcings = "TNF",
                                conditions = doses, equilibrate = TRUE, reduceCQ = TRUE, reconstruct = TRUE,
                                cores = getOption("dMod2.cores"))
symmetries <- readRDS("results/symmetries.rds")
symmetries
#> Result:  rank 71 / 79  |  8 non-identifiable directions
#> 
#> Generators  X = Σᵢ ξ(i) ∂ᵢ
#> 
#> Scalings:
#>   X₁  (exact)
#>       ξ(act_Ikk_by_TNF) :  + act_Ikk_by_TNF
#>       ξ(uptake)         :  - uptake
#> 
#>   X₂  (exact)
#>       ξ(act_Ikb_by_Ikk) :  + act_Ikb_by_Ikk
#>       ξ(act_Nfk_by_Ikk) :  + act_Nfk_by_Ikk
#>       ξ(s_pIKK)         :  + s_pIKK

#> 
#>   X₃  (exact)

#> exact = proven over Q.

The rank of the observability-identifiability matrix is 71 of 79 coordinates, proven; the kernel is spanned by eight scalings, each proven over the rationals. The eight printed generators are one basis, sums of them are symmetries too. Up to such sums there are four kinds.

  • Unobserved intermediates. Active receptor TNFR, IκBα transcript mIkb, A20 transcript and A20 protein are unmeasured, A20 only up to a scale. Each acts through the product of level and driven rate constant: level and production rate times \(\lambda\), driven rate divided by \(\lambda\). \(X_1\): receptor (uptake, act_Ikk_by_TNF); \(X_4\): IκBα transcript (prod_mIkb_by_nNfk, prod_Ikb); \(X_6\): A20 transcript (build_RnaA20, build_A20). \(X_7\) moves A20 with the A20 production, the IKK inhibition constant inh_Ikk (entering as A20 / inh_Ikk) and the scale of the A20 imaging readout.
  • Relative measurements. Blots and imaging give no absolute amounts. \(X_2\) divides the IKK total and every IKK form by \(\lambda\) and multiplies the IKK-catalyzed phosphorylation rates and the pIKK blot scale by \(\lambda\); the IKK cycle is linear in IKK. NFκB and IκBα scale together: every form times \(\lambda\); complex formation (second order), the readout scales and the A20 transcription driven by nuclear NFκB divided by \(\lambda\). The printed \(X_3\) is this direction plus \(X_4\) and \(X_5\), hence it also moves nuclear volume and IκBα production.
  • Nuclear volume. In \(X_5\) Vnuc grows at fixed amounts, nuclear concentrations fall, and the rates reading them (transcription of IκBα and A20, nuclear complex formation) and the scale of nuclear NFκB grow to compensate.
  • A product. split_NfkIkb appears only multiplied by eta_split_pNfkpIkb (\(X_8\)).

Symmetry reduction

symmetryReduction() returns in $trafo a parameter transformation that removes the directions, for scalings by fixing one coordinate per direction (Methods > Gauge and reduction).

# a section of every orbit of the scalings
reduction <- symmetryReduction(symmetries, timeout = 120)
reduction <- readRDS("results/reduction.rds")
reduction
#> Reduced 8 of 8 directions.
#> 
#> Trafo (non-identity entries)
#>   act_Ikb_by_Ikk     = 1
#>   act_Ikk_by_TNF     = 1
#>   build_RnaA20       = 1
#>   eta_split_pNfkpIkb = 1
#>   form_complex       = 1
#>   inh_Ikk            = 1
#>   prod_Ikb           = 1
#>   s_nucNFkB          = 1
#> 
#> Sections:
#>   {X₁}                  act_Ikk_by_TNF = 1
#>   {X₂}                  act_Ikb_by_Ikk = 1
#>   {X₃, X₄, X₅, X₆, X₇}  form_complex = 1, s_nucNFkB = 1, inh_Ikk = 1, prod_Ikb = 1, build_RnaA20 = 1
#>   {X₈}                  eta_split_pNfkpIkb = 1
#>   summary(x, detailed = TRUE) explains each section.

Gauge fixing

The objective is flat along every orbit, so the fit fixes one moved coordinate per symmetry, the gauge. This chooses units and leaves the fit unchanged. model.R fixes one parameter per scaling at 1, 0 on log scale:

# one coordinate of each scaling (symmetries.R) fixed at 1, at 0 on the log scale
gauge <- c(Vnuc = 0, totalNfk = 0, totalIkk = 0, uptake = 0, prod_Ikb = 0, build_RnaA20 = 0,
           split_NfkIkb = 0, s_A20GFP = 0)

The eight coordinates remove all eight scalings if their weight matrix is regular (Methods > Gauge and reduction):

W <- t(vapply(symmetries$symmetries, function(X)
  vapply(names(gauge), function(cn) as.numeric(X$weights[[cn]] %||% 0), 0), numeric(length(gauge))))
dimnames(W) <- list(paste0("X", seq_len(nrow(W))), names(gauge))
W
#>    Vnuc totalNfk totalIkk uptake prod_Ikb build_RnaA20 split_NfkIkb s_A20GFP
#> X1    0        0        0     -1        0            0            0        0
#> X2    0        0       -1      0        0            0            0        0
#> X3    1        1        0      0        1            0            0        0
#> X4    0        0        0      0        1            0            0        0
#> X5    1        0        0      0        0            1            0        0
#> X6    0        0        0      0        0           -1            0        0
#> X7    0        0        0      0        0            0            0       -1
#> X8    0        0        0      0        0            0           -1        0
det(W)
#> [1] -1

This is the gauge of Oppelt et al. [1]: NFκB and IKK totals and nuclear volume set the concentration units, so a concentration is a fraction of the moiety total; receptor and A20 transcript are in units of their production rates, the IκBα transcript in units of the translation it drives, A20 in units of the A20 imaging scale. The reduction fixes other coordinates, a different choice of units. Optimization fits the remaining 63 parameters, Profile likelihood checks which the data determine.

Reference: symmetryDetection(), symmetryReduction()
